tool_usage.tool_name: MediaTek DaVinci (達哥) + GPT-4 / Azure OpenAI IDE integration
how_used: other - code suggestion / generation / automatic error fixing inside the dev IDE
what_for: code suggestion and code generation inside the software-development IDE
improving software developer productivity within the IC design flow
broader enterprise automation (PPT generation, technical docs, market analysis, HR resume screening) via the DaVinci platform
tool_usage.teams: Company-wide internal platform (DaVinci/達哥). Specific code-assist use sits within software development / IC design engineering. MediaTek's Software Engineering & Product Security division separately drives a Copilot-like 'smart software factory' goal.
tool_usage.scale: Reported 97% of MediaTek employees have used DaVinci, 88% of users reported productivity gains, and it enabled 50+ cross-department GenAI projects (company-cited figures; caveat: self-reported, platform-wide not coding-specific). MediaTek has thousands of software engineers.
tool_usage.confidence_note: High confidence that MediaTek integrated GPT-4 (via Azure OpenAI) into its software-development IDE for code suggestion/generation/auto-fix - this exact claim appears in the Microsoft newsroom case study and is repeated by Business Weekly. The 97%/88%/50-project figures are company-cited and platform-wide (not coding-specific), so apply them to coding use only loosely.

tool_usage.tool_name: Domain-adapted LLM AI agents on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD (AI Factory)
how_used: other - AI-assisted code completion and automated technical documentation in R&D
what_for: AI-assisted code completion to reduce programming time and error rates
agentic extraction of information from design flowcharts and state diagrams to auto-generate technical documentation (days instead of weeks)
chip-design support: understanding, analyzing and optimizing designs
tool_usage.teams: R&D / engineering organization running on MediaTek's on-premises AI factory (Tongluo, Taiwan).
tool_usage.scale: AI factory processes ~60 billion tokens/month for inference and thousands of model-training iterations/month; scaled from 7B-parameter to 480B+-parameter model training in the same one-week window (attributed to Co-COO/CFO David Ku). Coding-agent seat/headcount numbers not disclosed.
tool_usage.confidence_note: High confidence on the use cases (AI-assisted code completion + documentation agents) and infrastructure scale - stated in NVIDIA's official customer story and MediaTek's own blog. These are home-grown domain-adapted LLM agents, not a named commercial coding agent. No per-engineer adoption figures disclosed.

what_for: auto-completing code lines from partial engineer input (described as the model MediaTek wants to emulate to become a 'smart software factory')
tool_usage.teams: MediaTek Software Engineering and Product Security Division.
tool_usage.scale: unknown - no confirmed seat counts or deployment scale; framed as a plan 'similar to' Copilot rather than a confirmed Copilot product rollout.
tool_usage.confidence_note: Low confidence / weak source. GitHub Copilot is referenced as an analogy/target for MediaTek's internal code-completion ambitions, not as confirmed evidence that the commercial GitHub Copilot product is deployed across MediaTek with measurable seats.

notes: MediaTek's agentic/AI coding usage is internal_dev (dogfooding of home-built tooling on top of GPT-4/Azure OpenAI and NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD), not adoption of brand-name agentic coding agents. Concrete confirmed coding use cases: code suggestion/generation/auto-fix in the dev IDE, AI-assisted code completion in R&D, and agentic auto-generation of technical documentation from design diagrams. No evidence found of Claude Code, Cursor, Devin, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Amazon Q Developer, OpenAI Codex/Operator, Antigravity, or Cowork at MediaTek; GitHub Copilot appears only as an aspirational reference. Caveat: WebFetch hit HTTP 403 on most domains, so usage details rely on verbatim WebSearch snippets from the cited primary/credible pages; publication dates unverified. DaVinci was reportedly spun out/transferred to Cyberon (賽微科技) in early 2025.
